Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis

Details: The failing test `testCpioUnarchiveCreatedByRedlineRpm` attempts to read a CPIO archive created by Redline RPM. The current bug report states that Redline RPM produces CPIO archives with a non-zero file mode on the trailer entry, which triggers an IllegalArgumentException when reading. 

Looking at the code of CpioArchiveInputStream.getNextEntry() and subsequently getNextCPIOEntry(), the method reads the next entry in the archive. It calls different read*Entry methods based on the archive format. For the "new" format, it calls readNewEntry(boolean).

Inspecting readNewEntry(boolean) reveals that it reads various pieces of information from the input stream, including the file mode. It sets the mode on the CpioArchiveEntry only if it's non-zero. After reading the name of the entry, it throws an IOException if the mode is zero for any entry other than the trailer (name not equal to CPIO_TRAILER). This enforces the condition that mode zero is only allowed for the trailer entry; other entries must have a non-zero mode.

However, the bug report states that Redline RPM violates the expected format by assigning a non-zero mode to the trailer entry. The current code treats this as illegal and results in an exception during archive extraction. Because the test archive "redline.cpio" was created by Redline RPM and includes a trailer with non-zero mode, getNextCPIOEntry() implementation is likely to raise the exception when it processes the trailer entry.

Thus, the root cause is this strict validation in readNewEntry that disallows trailer entries from having non-zero mode, while Redline RPM produces archives that do not follow this expectation. This causes the IllegalArgumentException or IOException when reading such archives.

No relevant fixes or patches are indicated in the recent bug reports. The diagnosis clearly shows the conflict between the Redline RPM archive format and the strict mode validation in readNewEntry.

This explains the failure of the test reading the Redline RPM generated archive, and the source of the IllegalArgumentException.

The likely fix would be to relax or adapt the mode validation logic in readNewEntry or in getNextCPIOEntry to allow trailer entries to have non-zero mode as per Redline RPM's behavior.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
